Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: The grandparent notices their grandchild seems to be feeling lost or discouraged about a personal matter.
Situation2: They interact warmly with a long line of shoppers during a busy lunch hour.
Story: I stand behind the register, scanning groceries as quickly as I can, offering a smile and a kind word to each customer. The line stretches past the bakery, and I can feel the impatience simmering. My manager expects me to keep things moving, to be efficient and cheerful, no matter how tired I am. But today, my mind keeps drifting to my granddaughter, who sits quietly at the end of the counter, waiting for my shift to end. I saw her eyes, red-rimmed and distant, when she arrived. She’s always been so bright, but lately, she’s withdrawn, and I know she needs me—needs my stories, my reassurance, my wisdom. Yet every time I try to catch her gaze, another customer steps forward, demanding my attention. I want to reach out, to offer her comfort, but I can’t abandon my post. The pressure builds inside me, torn between the needs of the strangers in front of me and the silent plea of the child I love most.
